dylan: Heads-up — saw a persistent tail-latency spike on the vector-match endpoint during yesterday's 10k qps replay. Dropping raw numbers + a few traces. Can we sanity-check methodology before we start flipping kernels?

liya: Thanks. Do you have the exact harness config and whether this was replay or synthetic? Those dicts change batching behavior a lot.

dylan: Replay of production traffic (match-job-2026-03-14). Harness command I used: 
```
./replay-harness --source=s3://replays/match-2026-03-14 --qps=10000 --duration=30m --preserve-timestamps --concurrency=250
```
Summary from the run (perf-bot posted): p50 11ms p95 48ms p99 220ms p999 870ms. Tail looks correlated to KV cache misses during warmup waves.

perf-bot: synthetic-run-complete: id=run-176543, qps=10000, p50=11.3ms, p95=47.6ms, p99=221ms, p999=872ms, dropped=0 :robot_face:

jason: I pulled two flamegraphs from the same window (attached to the thread). High-level: a bunch of scheduling stalls in the batcher + multiple kernel context switches during KV cache population. My hunch: kernel selection changed around the same deploy — we may be picking a lower-throughput kernel that has worse tail for short sequences.

sasha: Noted. The rerank workload mixes a ~32-token query with many ~1k-token docs. KV cache gets churned because prefix lengths vary; that causes cache eviction churn and sudden longer KV loads. We should test with fixed payloads first (all 128d vectors, then 512d) to isolate vector-dim vs sequence-length effects.

maria: Proposal for a minimal, repeatable methodology (3 steps):
  1) Replay baseline with production trace (preserve timestamps).
  2) Synthetic sweep: single-dim and single-payload-size sweeps (vector dims: 128/256/512, payload sizes: small/medium/large), batching params grid.
  3) Profile the regressing windows with kernel-level traces + flamegraphs. Capture kernel selection decisions.

liya: Agree. Small practical checklist for the synthetic sweep:
```
# baseline synthetic config (JSON)
{
  "qps": 10000,
  "concurrency": 250,
  "vector_dim": 512,
  "payload_tokens": 32,
  "batch_max_tokens": 8192,
  "batch_timeout_ms": 8,
  "kernel_policy": "auto:latency"
}
```
Run the sweep with batch_max_tokens in [4096,8192,16384] and batch_timeout_ms in [4,8,12]. Keep other variables fixed.

jason: Also add an explicit kernel selector flip in the matrix: env KERNEL_SELECTOR=throughput vs latency vs cost. We saw a kernel permutation on Friday that swapped matmul-optimized-v2 -> fused-attn that increased p999 by ~2x for short sequences in my lab tests.

sasha: Quick note on metrics: use p50/p95/p99/p999 + bundle average kernel-switch counts per 5s slice. If kernel_switches > 0 in high-tail windows, mark them for rollback.

ops-bot: captured: trace-ids [trace-176543-1, trace-176543-2, trace-176543-3] uploaded to s3://perf-traces/1765432100/

dylan: I attached two sample request/response pairs where tail jumps. Both show a cache-prefix miss followed by a 2x longer KV fetch and an immediate kernel preemption.

maria: For the KV behavior experiment, do three runs: cold-start (empty KV), warm-start (preload top 10k prefixes), and mixed (10% new keys per minute). That should show how eviction/interleaving affects tail.

liya: I'll run the synthetic grid tonight and add a replay run with the kernel selector forcibly set to the previous stable value. Will post the comparison table.

jason: Two quick commands to toggle kernels in the runtime cluster for the controlled runs:
```
kubectl set env deploy/serve-runtime KERNEL_SELECTOR=latency
kubectl set env deploy/serve-runtime KERNEL_SELECTOR=throughput
```
Also capture /metrics/kernel_selector_decisions and the kernel runtime histogram.

sasha: One more data point: vector-dim scaling. For rerank, increasing vector_dim from 128->512 reduced compute efficiency on some kernels but actually lowered p95 (less vector noise). Weird. We need the sweep to confirm.

dylan: OK — next steps captured: liya -> synthetic grid + kernel flip tonight; maria -> kv behavior triple-run; jason -> attach flamegraphs and kernel traces; sasha -> run vector-dim narrow sweep. We'll reconvene when we have the table (aim: tomorrow morning). Thanks :thumbsup:
